title: Failure of bounded tree-size representation
statement: Let $\ell,T:\mathbb{N}\to\mathbb{N}$, let $n_0$ be a natural number, and suppose $\ell(n)\le n$ for every $n$. Let $F_n$ be a Boolean function on assignments to $\ell(n)$ inputs. Assume that every tree circuit on $\ell(n_0)$ inputs of size at most $T(n_0)$ disagrees with $F_{n_0}$ on some assignment. Then the language accepted by the padded circuits has no family of tree circuits whose size at length $n$ is at most $T(n)$ and which recognizes that language exactly.
